mockup_note: NO SCREEN. The numbers behind the shoot window change; the window card itself was locked under features/shoot-plan-you-can-actually-see. 04-preview/workflow-prediction.md states what the numbers become.
notes: Every visit window in the system was a day short, on every campaign, silently.
the_bug: contracts.posting_date is a Postgres DATE — a calendar day. The pg driver hands it to Node as a Date built at LOCAL midnight, which in India is 6:30pm UTC the day before. UTC arithmetic on it then lands a day early: stored 30 Aug -> received 29 Aug 18:30Z -> minus 2 days in UTC -> 27 Aug, when 28 Aug was meant. Also toISOString().slice(0,10) returned the 29th for a value that is the 30th.
why_local_getters: The driver builds the Date at midnight in the process timezone. On IST it is 29 Aug 18:30Z and .getDate() is 30; on UTC (Render) it is 30 Aug 00:00Z and .getDate() is 30. Local getters give the stored day on BOTH. The UTC getters agree only on one of them — and not the one the code was written on.
two_things_fixed_on_the_way: THE DEAD BRANCH. The window's second rule read content_end_date, which nothing in either app has ever written. The wizard writes window_end. So the rule never fired and the window fell through to the campaign end or a year-out ceiling. The comment recording this had sat in campaignRollup.service.js since it was written, about a different consumer, and nobody carried it across.

THE BOUNDARY COMPARISON. A slot is an instant; the window is calendar days. Comparing in UTC refused a 9am visit on the last allowed day, because 9am IST is 3:30am UTC the NEXT day — the same off-by-one wearing different clothes.
rule_change_approved: PRE_VISIT_BUFFER_DAYS_AGAINST_POSTING 2 -> 1. With a 7-day minimum on a set and invitations closing 3 days before the post, a 2-day buffer left no day at all for the visit.
deliberately_not_done: NO GLOBAL DRIVER CHANGE. Turning every DATE column into a string is the tidier fix and would have touched 30 columns across 16 tables — follower bookings, meal orders, subscriptions, payment config. The arithmetic bug is confined to ONE function, and that is what was fixed. The phone was already correct: DateField.parseISO builds a calendar day from its parts deliberately.

verification.against_production: Run against all six live contracts. A post due 10 Sep now gives 31 Aug -> 9 Sep — exactly one day before the post, which is the rule. The sixth is correctly impossible: its post is due today.
verification.regression: shoot-plan 29/29, brief-to-signing 19/19, deliverables 19/19, usage-term 20/20, stage4-parcel 25/25, offers-parity 12/12, coupon 11/11. Mobile 48 suites / 565 tests.
verification.my_own_fixture_was_wrong: I wrote that 6pm UTC is already tomorrow in India and expected the 31st. Wrong — the turn is at 6:30pm, so 6pm UTC is 11:30pm the SAME day. The test caught my fixture, which is what a boundary test is for. Corrected, with the reason kept in the file.
verification.a_check_pinned_the_arithmetic: A check written yesterday asserted the literal expression latest.getTime() < earliest.getTime(), so it broke the moment that arithmetic correctly moved onto calendar days. It now asserts the flag and the reason exist, not how the comparison is spelled.
verification.a_check_passed_while_testing_nothing: toContain('r.window_end || r.content_end_date') was satisfied by EITHER of the two places the phrase appears, so breaking the branch condition alone stayed green. Both sites now asserted separately. Ninth time this session; every one found by mutation, none by reading.
